findings.claim: Product defect: toFahrenheit always passes its result through Math.round and has no precision input, so the caller gets a whole number without asking for one and cannot recover the lost fraction. By the code's arithmetic, toFahrenheit(37) is 98.6 before rounding and returns 99; toFahrenheit(21) is 69.8 and returns 70. This breaks V-2 directly and undermines V-3, because a traveller gets an error of up to 0.5°F with no sign that it happened. The directions also disagree: toCelsius does not round, and toCelsius(toFahrenheit(37)) is (99-32)*5/9, about 37.22 rather than 37. Neither function has a precision parameter, so the 'caller chooses the precision' part of V-2 is not implemented in either direction. toCelsius does at least return the unrounded value for the caller to round. I-1 still holds at its one input, and no active obligation covers V-2, so nothing in the obligation set catches this. These results come from reading the code; nothing was executed because this audit has no execution tool.
findings.cause: tofahrenheit conversion: result is always rounded to a whole number with no caller-chosen precision

findings.claim: Vacuous witness: I-1 is defined only at toFahrenheit(100), where c * 9 / 5 + 32 is exactly the integer 212. Any test limited to that claim gets the same result from a correct implementation, the current Math.round version, or a Math.ceil, Math.floor or Math.trunc version. A green I-1 therefore says nothing about fractional results, and it cannot detect the rounding at convert.ts line 1. The supplied mutant was not run; its survival is derived from the arithmetic at input 100 and assumes the witness asserts only what I-1 states, because the test source is not in the checkout.
findings.cause: i-1 witness: integer-valued sole input cannot distinguish exact conversion from any rounding implementation
